definition: The reward system is a brain system involved in producing rewarding effects and related behavior. In the packet, the mesocorticolimbic system is described as a major part of it, where dopamine release is linked with changes such as euphoria.

provenance.scope: Source record C28981; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not define the reward system as a general brain system that produces rewarding effects and related behavior; it only says the mesocorticolimbic system is a major component of the brain reward system and that dextroamphetamine induces dopamine release with effects such as euphoria.
The definition adds an explanatory summary that is broader than the packet’s wording and is not directly supported by the supplied text.
The definition’s first sentence (“The reward system is a brain system involved in producing rewarding effects and related behavior”) is not explicitly stated anywhere in the provided packet text.

The packet provided is a descriptor record for dextroamphetamine and mainly discusses dopamine release and euphoria within the mesocorticolimbic system; it does not present a learning-focused account of the “reward system.”

The definition attributes a general role (“producing rewarding effects and related behavior”) beyond what the packet specifically supports (it only mentions behavioral changes such as euphoria linked to dopamine release in the mesocorticolimbic system).
